youtube.title: WEDNESDAY WEBINARS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke hosts Kathryn Ennis-Carter and Jaspreet Boparai for a Council Watch webinar on legislation passed just before the general election, including the Local Government Systems Improvement Bill's repeal of the wellbeing clauses and its restrictions on councillor access to information. They trace the decades-long shift from Borough Council-style direct democracy to a corporate governance model, question the timing and motives behind amalgamation, and encourage listeners to consider standing for council seats as MPs move on. For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday. youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke and Marty Gibson dissect a turbulent week of election theatre, from the two major parties' campaign launches to a poll putting the Greens at 16%. They debate what a Green-boosted left bloc might look like, growing unrest within National's ranks, the psychology behind activism and why strategic voting matters before registrations close, alongside listener feedback on vaccine injury and political burnout. For more information: Wednesday Webinars | Council Watch: Election Impact on Local Councils Ani O'Brien Substack | Should the centre right split their vote RCR's Special Focus | Election 2026 Coverage For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart examines the increasingly unclear circumstances surrounding the alleged terrorist incident at RAF Fairford in the UK, questioning the official account and the handling of the investigation. She also highlights a fiery TalkTV interview with presenter Alex Phillips, who challenges the UK’s defence and national security response. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X

youtube.title: CHANTELLE BAKER
youtube.summary: Independent journalist Chantelle Baker joins Paul Brennan to discuss strategic voting under MMP, explaining how splitting electorate and party votes can affect the balance of Parliament. They examine polling, electorate contests and overhangs. They also discuss Baker’s ongoing defamation case against Stuff over Fire and Fury , including the discovery process and jury trial. Discover more from Chantelle on X , Facebook and Instagram For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday

youtube.title: RCR Wednesday Webinars - Council Watch
youtube.summary: Join Maree Buscke & Kathryn Ennis-Carter for a timely discussion exploring the growing intersection between local government and the national political landscape. What could the next election mean for New Zealand’s local councils — and what should voters be watching? 🔹 Amalgamation: What does the government’s stalling mean for council costs and planning ahead of the 2026 elections? 🔹 Last-minute legislation: What changes could be pushed through before the election? 🔹 Local to national: Which councillors could be looking to make the leap to Parliament? With local government increasingly connected to the wider political agenda, this is a conversation about who is making the decisions, where power is moving, and what voters should be watching.

youtube.title: MONEY TALKS
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan and Joel Robinson of Radical Investment explore why rising US bond yields matter, explaining the inverse relationship between interest rates and bond prices and the growing risks around long-duration debt. They examine warning signs emerging in AI-related debt markets, the disconnect between bonds and shares, and lessons from previous market cycles, while Joel discusses ways investors can reduce exposure to potential volatility and remain focused on long-term strategy.
